Product Changelog Timeline

What's new

Everything we've shipped, newest first. Currently on version 1.0, in App Store review.

Screenshots show the app as it looks today.

1 August 2026 Latest
  • You choose what you're notified about. Five kinds of alert, each with its own switch. Nothing is turned on behind your back.
  • The app asks if a plan happened. A few hours afterwards, so you don't have to remember to tell it.
  • You'll know when a plan is cancelled, and why. Before, plans just quietly vanished.
  • Share where you are. Around the time of a plan, with one tap. It's deleted when the plan's over.
  • Put something on it. Both of you can stake points on a plan happening. Turn up and you both get them back.
  • See who actually shows up. Built from plans that happened, not opinions. Partners can't see each other's.
  • Invite someone to a single plan. A code that gets them into that plan only — not your group, and nothing after it.
  • Suggested places when you say where you're meeting, instead of typing it out.
  • A weekly nudge if you haven't planned anything with someone in a while. Once a week at most, and never when you've already got something booked.
  • Suggesting a new time now works properly — say "Sunday instead?" and if they agree, the plan moves.
  • Fixed the number on the app icon, which was missing plans waiting on you.
  • Fixed screens flashing empty before loading, and rebuilt the plan screen, which was cramped.
31 July 2026
  • Submitted version 1.0 to the App Store.
  • "Did it happen?" The app now asks after a plan. Everything about who's reliable is built on that one answer.
  • Cancelling asks why. The plan stays on the record instead of disappearing.
  • Calendar clash warnings before you agree to something. Your calendar stays on your phone.
  • Your progress survives a new phone — badges and history, not just the numbers.
  • Separate progress for different activities. Getting good at cooking isn't getting good at travel.
30 July 2026
  • Name your groups, each with its own invite code. With more than one group, the app could show the code for the wrong one.
  • Two new kinds of plan: dates, and low-key nights in.
  • One-tap plans for the things people ask constantly — what are we watching, what are we eating.
  • Saved plans are easy to find again, and a plan can carry a place that opens in Maps.
18 – 26 July 2026
  • The first versions people could use: making a plan, agreeing a time, accounts, and connecting with someone.
